name: Nancy Pollard
title: Professor
department: Robotics Institute and Computer Science Department
fitReason: Strong physically grounded perception and human-demonstration transfer opportunity: contact-aware 3D reconstruction, retargeting across embodiments and sensor-based robot correction. The verified bathing study is principally reconstruction/optimization and reactive control, not a newly trained neural manipulation policy.

physicalEvidence.summary: August 10, 2026 primary paper transfers captured human demonstrations to an actual xArm 7 with a DexKit soft hand and tactile glove. It combines SMPL-X/MANO/MoSh++ and TRAM-based reconstruction, contact retargeting and tactile pressure correction. Hardware trials bathe a static mannequin, with the human trajectory slowed 20×. The authors explicitly state the system is not ready for human-subject deployment and report geometry mismatch, force-distribution and finger-curling limitations.

shortVisit.summary: Current official faculty and lab pages verify an active group but no external short-term visitor invitation. Internal CMU summer-undergraduate support and historical graduate supervision do not establish an external-master’s summer 2027 opportunity.

scoreReasons.fit: 37/40: concrete contact-aware 3D reconstruction and demonstration transfer; more geometric/feedback-control than current neural policy learning.
scoreReasons.physical: 25/25: directly documented 2026 real xArm/soft-hand execution, with mannequin and safety limitations explicit.
scoreReasons.shortVisit: 0/20: no current external visiting-master’s route established.
